source.work: Node.js documentation, blocking versus non-blocking calls
source.paraphrase: Sync filesystem and child-process calls block the event loop until they finish. Server code uses the async variants.

invariants.why: A sync call stops every request on that process while the disk or child answers.
invariants.fixHint: Use the promises variant and await it, or move the work off the request path.
invariants.avoid: Destructuring the function off its module still blocks. A helper whose name ends in Sync is still this call.

source.paraphrase: Libraries report failure by throwing or setting the exit code. Only the entry point decides when the process ends.

invariants.why: A library that exits kills the host CLI, test runner, or server without cleanup.
invariants.fixHint: Throw, return a failure, or set process.exitCode and return.
invariants.avoid: Reading the exit code first does not excuse calling exit. A branch around the call is still a call.

source.paraphrase: The environment is input to the process. Code reads it at startup and never rewrites it at runtime.

invariants.why: A write changes every module in the process and leaks between tests.
invariants.fixHint: Read the value into a local and pass it down. Keep test overrides in the test setup.
invariants.avoid: Bracket access is the same write. A defaulting operator still assigns.

source.paraphrase: Builtin imports carry the node: prefix so they cannot be confused with packages on disk.

invariants.why: A bare specifier resolves against packages first, so a new dependency can shadow the builtin.
invariants.fixHint: Write the specifier with the node: prefix, including subpaths.
invariants.avoid: A dynamic import needs the prefix too. A similarly named package is not the builtin.

source.paraphrase: The Buffer constructor is deprecated because a number argument leaves memory uninitialized. Factories state the intent.

invariants.why: A size argument can expose old heap contents to the next reader.
invariants.fixHint: Use the from factory for data and alloc for zeroed memory.
invariants.avoid: A comment naming the factory does not replace the call. A size argument is still this constructor.

source.paraphrase: The legacy parser is frozen and kept for compatibility. New code parses with the WHATWG URL class.

invariants.why: The legacy shape differs from the standard URL, so parsing moves behavior callers do not expect.
invariants.fixHint: Construct a URL and read its fields.
invariants.avoid: Passing the query flag stays on the legacy parser. Another parse function is not this call.
